category_overview: These six tools span IDE assistants (GitHub Copilot, Gemini Code Assist, Amazon Q Developer), an AI-native editor (Cursor), a terminal/cloud coding agent (Claude Code) and the open-source test framework (Playwright) that all of them now drive through MCP servers and agent definitions. They compete head-on in agentic multi-file coding, automated PR review and enterprise controls, and increasingly resell the same frontier models: Copilot and Cursor offer Claude, GPT and Gemini, while Claude Code itself runs inside VS Code and Cursor and on Bedrock, Google Cloud Agent Platform and Microsoft Foundry. 2026 was a consolidation year: Google stopped selling Code Assist (Oct 9) in favour of Antigravity, AWS announced Q Developer's retirement for Kiro (Apr 30 2027), SpaceX folded Cursor into a Grok bundle (Oct 12), and GitHub moved to usage-metered AI Credits (June 1). Enterprises typically standardise on GitHub Copilot where GitHub is already the SCM, add Claude Code or Cursor for agentic work, keep the hyperscaler assistant matching their primary cloud, and adopt Playwright with its MCP server as the neutral QA layer. Procurement now has to track usage-based metering and model-provider retention terms as closely as seat prices.

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.vendor: Anthropic (Claude product family). Bundled in Claude Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise; also pay-as-you-go via Anthropic Console, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Agent Platform (renamed from Vertex AI) and Microsoft Foundry.
tools.what_it_is: Agentic coding tool that reads a codebase, edits files, runs commands and opens pull requests. Surfaces: terminal CLI, VS Code and JetBrains extensions, desktop app, web (claude.ai/code) and mobile, plus Slack, GitHub Actions/GitLab CI and an Agent SDK.
key_capabilities: Multi-file edits under permission modes: auto (a classifier screens actions), manual, sandboxed bash
Subagents, dynamic workflows and a Projects coordinator for long-running parallel work
CLAUDE.md memory, skills, hooks, plugins and MCP connectors
GitHub Code Review (GA Oct 2026) with Quick/Standard/Deep levels
Scheduled routines, Remote Control, cloud sessions and CLI piping for CI and log triage
tools.enterprise_data_handling: Team, Enterprise, API and cloud-provider deployments: Anthropic does not train on code or prompts unless the org opts into the Development Partner Program; 30-day retention; zero data retention available to qualified Enterprise accounts. Free/Pro/Max: training only if the user enables it (5-year retention on, 30 days off). Enterprise adds SSO, SCIM, RBAC, audit logs, compliance API, custom retention, IP allowlisting, CMEK, US-only inference and a HIPAA-ready offering with BAA; managed settings enforce policy. SOC 2 Type 2 report and ISO 27001 certificate are published via the Anthropic Trust Center.
tools.licensing_pricing: USD: Pro $20/month ($17 annual); Max $100 or $200/month; Team Standard seat $25/month or $20 annual (2-seat minimum), Premium seat $125/$100; Enterprise $20/seat/month billed annually (20-seat self-serve, 50-seat sales-assisted minimum) plus all usage at API rates with no included tokens. Not bundled with any office suite.
tools.integrations: Git, GitHub, GitLab, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI/CD, Slack, Chrome debugging, OpenTelemetry, MCP servers (Jira, Google Drive, Datadog, PagerDuty, Zapier, Workato, Notion, Asana), LLM gateways.
tools.recent_developments: May 2026 Code with Claude: auto-mode classifier, worktrees, routines, Managed Agents, doubled rate limits. Sept 17 2026: Claude Code Projects coordinator. Oct 15 2026: Code Review GA with $10k Enterprise credits claimable to Jan 15 2027. Oct 23 2026 v2.1.310: Enterprise custom roles for cloud sessions, auto mode on Foundry. Rename flag: Vertex AI is now Google Cloud Agent Platform; vendor pages moved from anthropic.com to claude.com.
tools.best_fit_departments: Strong: 41, 42 (test generation with the Playwright agent loop), 44 (log piping, MCP runbooks), 49 and 51 (Agent SDK, workflows). 43 fits for IaC but lacks the native cloud cost analysis Amazon Q or Azure Copilot provide.
tools.training_notes: Master permission modes and auto-mode risk, CLAUDE.md, plan-then-execute, diff review, MCP trust, sandboxing and usage monitoring. Core 8-10 h (41); Advanced 14-18 h (42, 44); Specialist 24-32 h (43, 49, 51: Agent SDK, Bedrock/Foundry deployment, OpenTelemetry).
tools.caveats: Enterprise usage is metered at API rates, so spend limits matter; subscriptions have 5-hour usage windows. Vendor states no system is immune to prompt injection. Projects worker threads are cloud-only. Auto mode is default on Pro/Max/Team; feature availability differs by provider; supported-countries list applies.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.vendor: GitHub (Microsoft subsidiary). Copilot family: Free, Pro, Pro+, Max for individuals; Business and Enterprise for organisations.
tools.what_it_is: AI pair programmer and coding agent inside VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Neovim, Eclipse and Xcode, on GitHub.com, GitHub CLI, GitHub Mobile and Windows Terminal. Multi-model: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and xAI models are selectable per task.
key_capabilities: Completions and Next Edit Suggestions (not credit-metered) plus agent mode in the IDE
Cloud coding agent that turns issues into pull requests; Copilot code review
Copilot Spaces for shared context; custom agents, instructions and MCP servers with allow lists
Agentic autofix for code-scanning alerts (GA Oct 2026); local sandboxing; computer use for desktop apps
Usage metrics API covering custom skills, agents and MCP servers
tools.enterprise_data_handling: GitHub Terms (effective Apr 27 2026): the clause letting GitHub train on inputs and outputs applies only to individual licences (opt-out in account settings); Business/Enterprise use is governed by the GitHub Customer Agreement and Data Protection Agreement, and the product page lists IP indemnity and data privacy for both tiers. Admin policy management, content exclusions, audit logs and MCP allow lists. GitHub holds zero-data-retention agreements with OpenAI, Google, xAI and Anthropic, except Claude Fable 5/5.1 where Anthropic retains data by default for safety (enterprises can request ZDR through 2026). Compliance attestations are listed on the GitHub Enterprise Trust Center.
tools.licensing_pricing: USD monthly: Free $0; Pro $10 (1,500 AI Credits); Pro+ $39 (7,000); Max $100 (20,000); Business $19 per granted seat (1,900 credits); Enterprise $39 per seat (3,900). Since June 1 2026 usage is metered in GitHub AI Credits at $0.01 each, consumed by token usage per model; completions stay unmetered. Not bundled with Microsoft 365; purchasable under Microsoft Product Terms.
tools.integrations: GitHub repositories, issues, pull requests and Actions; Microsoft Teams notifications; MCP servers; Visual Studio, VS Code and JetBrains; multi-vendor model catalogue.
tools.recent_developments: Apr 27-28 2026: AI Credits announced, live June 1 2026, replacing premium requests; Business/Enterprise received $30/$70 promotional credits through August. Oct 2026 changelog: computer use, local sandboxing GA, Gemini 4 Argon and Claude Haiku 5.5 added, dynamic workflows in Copilot CLI, model deprecations Oct 19 and mid-November, global feature defaults GA.
tools.best_fit_departments: Strong: 41, 42, 53 (Spaces for ADRs, org-wide indexing) and 52 prototyping. Moderate: 43, 44, 49 - no cloud-specific troubleshooting or cost tooling; relies on MCP connectors to observability and data platforms.
tools.training_notes: Learn instruction files, agent mode versus cloud agent, reviewing agent PRs, credit budgeting and model choice. Core 6-8 h (41); Advanced 12-16 h (42, 52); Specialist 20-24 h (43, 44, 49, 53: policy admin, metrics API, MCP governance).
tools.caveats: Token-based credits make spend hard to predict (analyst warning); admins must set limits. Frequent model deprecations. Fable retention nuance. The Copilot Trust Center is script-rendered, so specific certifications and the 28-day retention figures circulated online were not verifiable here. Individual tiers allow training unless opted out.

tools.name: Gemini Code Assist
tools.vendor: Google (Google Cloud, 'Gemini for Google Cloud' family). Rename/sunset flag: Google now sells agentic coding as Google Antigravity inside Gemini Enterprise editions.
tools.what_it_is: Enterprise AI coding assistant for VS Code, JetBrains, Android Studio, Cloud Shell Editor and Cloud Workstations, with GitHub pull-request review and the Gemini CLI. Sold as Standard and Enterprise editions; the Individuals tier shut down June 18 2026.
key_capabilities: Code completion, generation, chat with open-file context and smart actions
Agent mode (GA July 2025) for multi-step edits and commands; auto-approve preview
Enterprise code customization from private GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket repos with CMEK
Google Cloud hooks: Firebase, BigQuery data insights, Cloud Run, Database Studio; Enterprise adds Apigee, Application Integration and Gemini Cloud Assist
GitHub Enterprise code review with persistent memory; release channels; Cloud console admin
tools.enterprise_data_handling: Standard and Enterprise: Google states Gemini for Google Cloud does not use prompts or responses to train models; private code is stored only to deliver customization; prompts are encrypted in transit; CMEK covers customization data. Source citations and IP indemnification are included. Licences are assigned through the Cloud console and IAM; agent admin controls entered preview Apr 2026. SOC/ISO/FedRAMP statements were not on the opened pages; the Google Cloud Data Processing Addendum applies.
tools.licensing_pricing: The official pricing page could not be parsed; an Oct 2025 independent review lists Standard $22.80 and Enterprise $54 per user per month (monthly; annual-commitment discounts not verified). New subscriptions unavailable since Oct 9 2026; licences can be added and annual plans renewed until Jan 31 2027, monthly plans until Dec 31 2027. Replacement Antigravity is included in Gemini Enterprise editions/Agent Platform and is free for individuals.
tools.integrations: Google Cloud (BigQuery, Cloud Run, Firebase, Apigee), GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket repositories, GitHub Enterprise PR reviews, MCP servers (replaced built-in tools Oct 2025), Gemini CLI GitHub Actions.
tools.recent_developments: Mar 13 2026: Gemini 3.1 Pro and 3.0 Flash preview; Jun 8 2026: Gemini 3.5 Flash GA. Jun 18 2026: Individuals and Google AI Pro/Ultra IDE tiers stopped, users sent to Antigravity. Oct 9 2026: end of sale for Standard/Enterprise. Docs now say Gemini CLI is not optimised for the latest models and point to Antigravity CLI.
tools.best_fit_departments: 43 Cloud (GCP-native teams) fits best while contracts run; 41 and 44 adequate via Cloud Assist; 42 weak (no dedicated test agents). Treat all as transitional and plan Antigravity training.
tools.training_notes: Agent-mode controls, customization scope, citation checking, Cloud console licensing. Core 6-8 h (41); Advanced 12 h (42, 44); Specialist 20 h for 43 GCP platform teams including migration to Antigravity CLI and IDE extensions.
tools.caveats: End of sale; no published price mapping to Gemini Enterprise; unclear whether code-customization settings transfer to Antigravity. Google advises validating outputs because plausible-but-wrong answers occur. New buyers cannot purchase either edition.

tools.name: Cursor
tools.vendor: Anysphere, Inc. d/b/a Cursor - a wholly owned SpaceX subsidiary since Aug 14 2026, now sold under SpaceX Super Intelligence's 'The X Subscription' by X Subscription Corp. The brief's 'Anysphere' is the legal entity but ownership changed.
tools.what_it_is: AI-native code editor with in-editor agents, cloud agents, Bugbot pull-request review and an iOS app. Models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and SpaceX AI (Grok). Since Oct 12 2026 it is sold in the same subscription as Grok and X Premium.
key_capabilities: Agent coding in-editor; Cloud Agents, Projects coordinator (Sept 2026), shareable Canvases
Bugbot code review plus Security Review and Rollouts bots (Teams/Enterprise)
Origin App Marketplace: Cloudflare, Linear, Sentry, Socket Security integrations
Remote Control of local agents from iOS; Environments API
Enterprise controls over models, MCP servers, repositories and spend
tools.enterprise_data_handling: Privacy Mode: Cursor will not train on customer data and holds zero-data-retention agreements with all model providers; file contents are cached only for the request. With Privacy Mode off, code and prompts may train Cursor models; opened docs do not state it is force-enabled for Teams/Enterprise. Enterprise: SAML SSO (Okta, Entra ID, Google), SCIM, audit logs, model/MCP/repository allowlists, AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+, CMEK, MDM. SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001:2022, ISO 42001:2023, AIUC-1; GDPR/CCPA. Cloud-only on AWS, no on-prem; no infrastructure in China.
tools.licensing_pricing: USD monthly under The X Subscription: Free $0; Plus $8 (Grok models only); Premium $30 (bundles former Cursor Pro, SuperGrok and X Premium+; third-party models billed at API rates); Super $100; Ultra $200; usage pools shared weekly across Grok and Cursor. Teams $30/$100/$200 per seat with SSO, admin and analytics. Enterprise custom via sales: invoice/PO, SCIM, audit logs, single usage pool. Existing Cursor plans may be kept.
tools.integrations: GitHub PRs (Bugbot), Slack triggers, Linear, Sentry, Cloudflare, Socket, MCP servers; the Claude Code extension installs in Cursor.
tools.recent_developments: Oct 2025: Cursor 2.0 parallel agents. Nov 2025: $2.3B Series D at $29.3B. Apr 21 2026: SpaceX purchase option; exercised Jun 16; closed Aug 14 2026. Oct 12 2026: The X Subscription replaces Cursor plans. Press reports OpenAI will cut Cursor's access to its models Nov 12 2026. Oct 2026: Canvases, Origin marketplace, Remote Control.
tools.best_fit_departments: 41 (the only listed department) fits well for application developers; weak for regulated teams needing on-prem deployment or stable vendor terms.
tools.training_notes: Agent mode, rules and skills, Privacy Mode verification, diff review, Bugbot triage, Cloud Agents and Projects. Core 6-10 h (41); Advanced 12-16 h for admins (controls, spend limits, model allowlists).
tools.caveats: Ownership, pricing and model-access churn; reported OpenAI cut-off; usage pools shared with Grok; cloud-only; Privacy Mode must be enforced by policy; Remote Control is on by default except on Enterprise.

tools.name: Playwright
tools.vendor: Microsoft (open source, Apache-2.0, github.com/microsoft/playwright). Not an AI SaaS; AI arrives through Playwright Test Agents, the Playwright MCP server and the optional Azure App Testing service (formerly Microsoft Playwright Testing).
tools.what_it_is: Browser automation and end-to-end test framework for Chromium, Firefox and WebKit in TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, .NET and Java, with a test runner, codegen and trace viewer. Since v1.56 it ships agent definitions and an MCP server that let coding assistants plan, write and heal tests.
key_capabilities: Auto-wait, retrying assertions, role-based locators, parallel sharding, isolated contexts
Test Agents Planner, Generator and Healer via 'npx playwright init-agents --loop=vscode|claude|codex|opencode'
Playwright MCP drives browsers through accessibility snapshots for Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot and VS Code
Trace viewer with aria snapshots, HAR recording, video, WebAuthn passkeys
v1.64: WebMCP testing, test locks, --shuffle, locator.within()
tools.enterprise_data_handling: The framework runs locally; no data goes to Microsoft. Agent and MCP traffic goes to whichever LLM client the team uses, so Copilot, Claude or Codex policies govern code exposure. Azure Playwright Testing (now part of Azure App Testing) stores reports for 90 days in the workspace region (East US, West US 3, East Asia, West Europe); Azure attestations were not verified here.
tools.licensing_pricing: Free, Apache-2.0. Azure App Testing is consumption-based ('pay only for what you use') with a free trial; per-minute rates were not on the opened page. LLM costs sit with the chosen assistant.
tools.integrations: VS Code (v1.105+ for agents), Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor and GitHub Copilot via MCP; Playwright MCP also configures for Windsurf, Cline and Goose; commercial Leapwork Play layer.
tools.recent_developments: v1.56 (Oct 2025) Test Agents; v1.57 Chrome for Testing builds and page.accessibility removed; v1.59 CLI debugger and dashboard for agents; v1.62 component-testing overhaul; v1.63 test locks, Ubuntu 20.04 dropped; v1.64 WebMCP (Oct 2026). MCP repo at 38.6k stars; Playwright Testing folded into Azure App Testing.
tools.best_fit_departments: 42 Quality Engineering is the core fit for automation scripts and defect triage; also useful to 41 for component tests.
tools.training_notes: Locators, fixtures, trace viewer, CI sharding and flaky-test triage, then agent loops and reviewing generated specs. Advanced 12-20 h (42); Specialist 20-30 h for framework owners running agents and MCP in CI.
tools.caveats: Agents need human review; Healer can mask real regressions. Enterprise orchestration, scheduling and audit sit outside the framework. Node 18 is deprecated from v1.54. GitHub shows relative release dates, so the Oct 2026 date for v1.64 is inferred from the version sequence.

tools.name: Amazon Q Developer
tools.vendor: Amazon Web Services. The brief's vendor is correct, but the IDE/CLI product is being retired in favour of Kiro, AWS's agentic development environment.
tools.what_it_is: AWS generative-AI assistant for developers in VS Code, JetBrains, Visual Studio and Eclipse plugins, the command line, the AWS Management Console and mobile app, Slack/Teams, and GitHub/GitLab Duo. IDE plugins, paid subscriptions and code transformation end Apr 30 2027; console and chat-app surfaces continue.
key_capabilities: Agentic coding: feature development, tests, docs, reviews, refactoring
Code transformation: Java version upgrades and .NET-to-Linux porting
Security scanning with remediation; AWS console error diagnosis, architecture and cost guidance
Private-repo customization; reference tracking and public-code suppression
Kiro successor: specs, hooks, steering files, MCP/ACP, property-based testing, parallel agents, Claude/GPT/open-weight models
tools.enterprise_data_handling: Free tier: questions, responses and generated code may be used for service improvement including model training unless opted out (IDE settings or an AWS Organizations AI opt-out policy). Pro tier: content is not used for improvement or FM training and is stored in the profile's region for IDE, CLI and console chat; other features store in US regions. SOC 1/2/3 reports via AWS Artifact; IAM Identity Center, admin dashboard and IP indemnity on Pro. Kiro Enterprise: content not used for improvement, customer-chosen region, CMEK option, TLS 1.2+; Kiro Free/individual content may be used.
tools.licensing_pricing: Q Developer: Free $0 (50 agentic requests/month, 1,000 Java lines); Pro $19/user/month (4,000 pooled lines, $0.003/line overage). New Free/Pro sign-ups blocked May 15 2026; Pro subscriptions work with Kiro but cannot revert. Kiro USD/month: Free 50 credits; Pro $20 (1,000); Pro+ $40 (2,000); Pro Max $100 (5,000); Power $200 (10,000); Enterprise custom; add-ons $0.04/credit; GovCloud about 20% higher. Not suite-bundled.
tools.integrations: AWS Console, CloudWatch investigations, Redshift generative SQL, Console-to-Code, GitHub, GitLab Duo, Slack, Teams; Kiro adds IAM Identity Center, Okta, Entra ID and MCP.
tools.recent_developments: Apr 30 2026 end-of-support blog: sign-ups blocked May 15 2026; Opus 4.6 removed from Pro May 29 2026; plugins, subscriptions and transformation end Apr 30 2027. Kiro expanded to IDE, CLI, web, mobile and open-source Kiro Crew with a multi-model Auto mode.
tools.best_fit_departments: 43 Cloud fits AWS-native teams (troubleshooting, IaC, cost guidance) but only until 2027; plan Kiro for coding work.
tools.training_notes: Console troubleshooting, IAM Identity Center setup and opt-out policies, then Kiro specs, hooks, steering and credit governance. Core 6-8 h for Q console users; Specialist 20-24 h for 43 platform teams migrating to Kiro.
tools.caveats: Sunset timeline; Kiro credits differ from Q's per-call metering; transformation features disappear; Free-tier training default; US-region processing for some features; feature parity not guaranteed; one independent source quotes Kiro at $19/$39 versus kiro.dev's $20/$40.
